overall_summary: Escalating US-Iran strikes and Hormuz closure dominate with clear risk-off pressure, amplified by Fed inflation warnings and sticky yields near 4.56 percent. Bitcoin ETFs managed a rare green week and price holds near power-law support, yet the macro and geopolitical backdrop favors caution heading into CPI. Overall tone remains defensive for crypto until levels resolve or data softens.
key_points: US-Iran strikes close Hormuz, elevating risk-off
Fed flags higher inflation from tariffs, war, AI
Bitcoin ETFs post first green week since May
BTC nears power-law support, still unresolved

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs Post First Green Week Since May
items.summary: US spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded their first weekly net inflows since May, capped by about ninety million dollars on July tenth led by BlackRock's IBIT and VanEck. After weeks of heavy outflows that drained billions, this marks a potential shift in institutional demand at prices near sixty-four thousand. Traders should care because sustained inflows act as a structural buyer and could stabilize or lift the market if they continue into next week.
items.impact: Supports price floor and rebound potential via institutional demand

items.title: Bitcoin Holds Steady Amid Fresh US Iran Strikes
items.summary: Bitcoin and ether barely budged after the US launched its third round of strikes on Iran this week and Tehran again closed the Strait of Hormuz. With stocks and oil markets closed for the weekend, crypto is the main market pricing the escalation yet prices stayed near sixty-three thousand eight hundred. Traders should note this muted reaction versus past geo shocks, as it may signal maturing risk tolerance, though Monday's oil open will test the calm.
items.impact: Shows resilience to geo risk; watch Monday oil reaction for spillover

items.title: Empery Digital Sells Half Its Bitcoin for AI Pivot
items.summary: Bitcoin treasury company Empery Digital sold roughly fourteen hundred BTC, about half its stack, at an average of sixty-two thousand two hundred for eighty-seven million dollars. Proceeds will fund debt repayment and a stake in a Midwest AI data center as the firm shifts away from pure treasury strategy and may sell more. This reflects a broader cooling of corporate BTC accumulation as capital rotates to AI, adding potential supply overhang for traders to monitor.
items.impact: Adds near-term supply and weakens treasury-buyer narrative

items.title: BIP-110 Soft Fork Nears Deadline With Near-Zero Support
items.summary: The BIP-110 proposal to temporarily restrict non-financial data on Bitcoin has under one percent miner signaling and low node adoption as its early August deadline looms. Michael Saylor and Adam Back publicly opposed it, warning that turning a spam debate into a consensus rule sets a dangerous precedent. With support this low it is unlikely to activate network-wide and would at most create a tiny minority chain, so the main Bitcoin network faces little disruption risk.
items.impact: Preserves status quo; low chance of protocol disruption

items.title: Ripple Nearly Shut Down Over SEC Fight, CEO Says
items.summary: Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse revealed that he and co-founder Chris Larsen seriously considered winding the company down and distributing its XRP to shareholders after the twenty-twenty SEC lawsuit rather than fight. They chose to battle, spending about one hundred fifty million in legal fees, and ultimately won a ruling that XRP itself is not a security. This retrospective highlights past existential regulatory risk for a major player and underscores how much the landscape has shifted.
items.impact: No immediate catalyst; reinforces regulatory survival narrative for alts

items.title: Bitcoin Nears Fidelity Power-Law Support Line
items.summary: Fidelity's Jurrien Timmer notes Bitcoin is approaching a long-term power-law support line the firm has tracked since two thousand fifteen, currently viewing the zone near sixty thousand as an accumulation area. While a catalyst for a strong bounce is still missing amid capital rotation into AI, the model frames this region as a potential floor after the drawdown. Technical traders will watch for a confirmed hold or bounce here as a possible basing signal.
items.impact: Flags key long-term support zone awaiting catalyst or resolution

items.title: Fed Report Flags Stepped-Up Inflation from Tariffs, Iran War, AI
items.summary: The Federal Reserve's semi-annual monetary policy report released Friday highlighted that inflation stepped up further this spring. It pointed to tariffs, higher energy costs from the Middle East conflict, and booming AI-related demand as key drivers, with PCE still roughly double the 2 percent target. Traders should care because this reinforces the case for holding rates higher or even hiking later this year, which typically pressures risk assets including Bitcoin as real yields stay elevated.
items.impact: Supports higher-for-longer rates, negative for risk assets

items.title: June CPI Data Drops Tuesday: Markets Eye Sticky Inflation
items.summary: The Consumer Price Index for June 2026 is due out Tuesday at 8:30 AM Eastern. Prediction markets are pricing a year-over-year print near or above 3.7 percent with high confidence it exceeds 3.6 percent. This is the key data point before the late-July FOMC, so a hot number would boost odds of a rate hike while a cool one could ease pressure. Crypto traders need to watch closely as it will set the tone for dollar, yields, and risk appetite heading into the week.
items.impact: High-volatility catalyst for rates and risk assets

items.title: Warsh Names High-Profile Leaders for Five Fed Task Forces
items.summary: New Fed Chair Kevin Warsh announced the leaders of five task forces examining communications, the balance sheet, data sources, productivity and AI jobs, and the inflation framework. Names include Marc Andreessen, former BoE Governor Mervyn King, Raghuram Rajan, and Nobel laureate Thomas Sargent. This signals potential major shifts in how the Fed operates and communicates, which could alter market expectations around policy transparency and the reaction function over the coming months.
items.impact: Increases uncertainty around long-term Fed framework

items.title: 10-Year Treasury Yield Holds Near 4.56 Percent
items.summary: The U.S. 10-year Treasury yield closed Friday around 4.56 percent and remains elevated heading into the weekend. Yields have been supported by sticky inflation concerns and reduced odds of near-term rate cuts. Higher long-term rates raise discount rates on future cash flows and often strengthen the dollar, both of which can weigh on Bitcoin and growth-sensitive assets until the next major data or Fed speak.
items.impact: Elevated yields pressure valuations and risk appetite

items.title: US Dollar Index Steady Near 101 Amid Rate Uncertainty
items.summary: The DXY finished Friday around 100.9 to 101, holding recent gains. Dollar strength has been underpinned by relative U.S. rate differentials and safe-haven flows tied to geopolitical risks. A firm greenback tends to act as a headwind for crypto prices denominated in dollars, so traders should monitor any break higher or lower around this week's inflation data.
items.impact: Strong dollar typically weighs on BTC and commodities

items.title: PPI and Beige Book Due Mid-Week After CPI
items.summary: Producer Price Index for June lands Wednesday alongside the Fed's Beige Book. These will fill out the inflation and regional activity picture right after CPI. With the next FOMC just weeks away and officials already divided, any signs of broadening price pressures could firm rate-hike pricing. Crypto markets often react to the full suite of inflation prints as they shape the real-yield outlook.
items.impact: Secondary inflation signals could reinforce or offset CPI move

items.title: US Strikes 140 Iran Targets; Hormuz Closed Again
items.summary: The United States hit about 140 Iranian military sites on Saturday in its third round of strikes this week after attacks on commercial shipping. Iran hit Gulf states including Qatar and declared the Strait of Hormuz closed until US interference ends, though the US says vessels still transit. Traders should watch this closely because the strait handles a fifth of global oil trade. Renewed disruption risks higher energy prices, inflation pressure, and a classic risk-off move that usually hits Bitcoin and equities first.
items.impact: Oil spike and risk-off pressure on crypto and stocks

items.title: Russian Strikes Kill Eight Across Ukraine
items.summary: Russia launched missiles and drones that killed at least eight people and wounded dozens, including strikes on Kyiv, Sumy and Odesa. Zelenskiy called for faster weapons deliveries from partners, noting critical shortages of interceptors for ballistic missiles. This keeps the Ukraine war hot and raises questions about Western support. For markets it sustains geopolitical risk premium and energy volatility from related infrastructure attacks.
items.impact: Sustained risk premium and energy supply worries

items.title: Ukraine Drone Hits Russian Tanker in Sea of Azov
items.summary: Russia says a Ukrainian drone struck an empty tanker entering the Azov-Black Sea Canal, with the fire controlled and no oil spill or casualties. Ukraine has intensified attacks on Russian fuel logistics and tankers near Crimea to disrupt supplies. This is part of a broader campaign that has already hit dozens of vessels. Traders care because it pressures Russian energy exports and can tighten global refined product markets.
items.impact: Potential tightness in fuel supplies, mixed energy prices

items.title: Joint Statement Rejects China's South China Sea Claims
items.summary: The United States, Japan, the Philippines and a dozen other countries issued a joint statement on the tenth anniversary of the 2016 arbitral ruling, reaffirming it is final and binding and that China's expansive claims have no legal basis. China continues to reject the award as null and void. This marks renewed diplomatic pushback in a flashpoint waterway. It raises the temperature on Indo-Pacific tensions that can affect shipping insurance, supply chains and risk assets.

items.title: US Senator Lindsey Graham Dies Suddenly at 71
items.summary: Longtime South Carolina Republican Senator Lindsey Graham, a key Trump ally and foreign-policy hawk who strongly backed Ukraine aid and tough stances on Iran, died from a brief sudden illness after returning from Ukraine. His death creates a Senate vacancy and removes a vocal interventionist voice. Markets watch for any shift in US foreign-policy consensus or defense spending debates that could influence risk sentiment.
items.impact: Potential shift in US foreign-policy dynamics

items.title: Former Qatari Emir Sheikh Hamad Dies at 74
items.summary: Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani, who modernized Qatar, seized power in 1995 and later handed rule to his son, has died. Qatar has played a central mediation role in US-Iran talks and Gulf security. His passing comes amid ongoing Hormuz tensions and attacks on Qatari territory. It could subtly affect Gulf diplomacy and energy coordination at a sensitive moment for oil markets.
items.impact: Possible ripple on Gulf mediation and energy diplomacy
